sources.note: No phonology of Giamina. The section re-lists the ~20 Giamina words with cognates in Luiseno-Cahuilla, Gabrielino, Serrano, Kern River (Tubatulabal), Mono, Ute-Chemehuevi, notes 'distortion' (hewe for wehe, ni-ku for mi-ki) and elicitation errors, and argues the list may be 'a dialectic branch or group co-ordinate with the major ones of the family', possibly 'a link between the Kern River and Southern California branches'. The paper's phonetic key (p. 236 fn.) includes a mark glossed 'accent', and two Giamina forms carry an apostrophe-like mark in the scanned (muut/muni', wi'ct) that in the 1…

sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: Nothing. The entire Giamina record is a 20-word list on p. 128 (tcupu 'house', hewe 'water', pohoim 'road', wadja 'mountain', madjindji 'across', pābahai 'no', xöxinil/xaxinil 'person', muut 'man', wi'ct 'woman', piāt 'deer', ni-ku, bal/bal-aku, bèkt, tabakwan, dab-iku, hahītcu/ahītciwa, em 'much', hüüka 'drink', mik'an 'kill'; numerals 1-6). page scan checked: vowel diacritics only, no accent marks. The words 'accent' and 'stress' do not occur anywhere in the text of the whole 1907 monograph; the general phonetic note (pp. 96-100) concerns consonant classes and the ö/ü vowels.
